## Simple explanation

A Tensor Core is a specialized hardware unit in some GPUs that accelerates
matrix calculations common in neural networks. It can perform these
operations faster than general-purpose compute units when the software and
data formats are compatible.

## Technical explanation

Tensor Cores accelerate matrix multiply-accumulate operations, often using
lower-precision input formats with higher-precision accumulation. Exact
supported formats and behavior depend on GPU generation, libraries, and
kernel selection.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Hardware acceleration can improve training throughput and inference
latency, but only when the workload maps to supported operations. Precision
choices also affect numerical error, memory use, and model quality.

## How it works

Optimized frameworks select kernels that partition matrix operations into
tiles and dispatch them to the accelerator. Developers can use mixed
precision or optimized libraries, then benchmark the complete workload and
check numerical behavior.

## Practical example

A neural network's large matrix multiplications may use a supported
lower-precision format on a GPU with Tensor Cores. Compare throughput and
validation metrics against a baseline before changing production settings.

## Common misconceptions

- Tensor Cores are not available or used for every operation or every GPU.
- Lower-precision execution does not guarantee a speedup if the workload is
  too small, memory-bound, or unsupported by optimized kernels.
